title: ENDEX: Storm Over, Restoration Queued, 06:00 CDT

fields.resolution: ENDEX. THIS IS AN EXERCISE. It is 06:00 CDT on Wednesday, 17 March 2027, four hours after STARTEX. NLTO's GMD operating procedure was terminated at the time logged on the supervisor's desk. The UMRC sent its termination and post-event data request at 04:20 CDT, and the termination notice reached all 14 entities. The final public statement and the state's 06:00 update give the same message. Please stop play now and move to the hot wash.
finalState: NLTO's short report is in draft. It leads with the 168 A peak neutral current on Iron Range T2.

Line HARTLEY–IRON RANGE 345-1 restoration and the six deferred 345 kV outages are queued in the order the Transmission Operations Manager set. Iron Range T2 is waiting on its oil sample result, due at 08:00.
The Hartley spare autotransformer and the AT-1 replacement are waiting on the heavy-haul permit (earliest move Tuesday 23 March) and a 120-ton crane slot (earliest Wednesday 24 March).
The Iron Range and Cloquet sites run on the Duluth network time source and their GPS receivers have no stable lock yet. Their original holdover deadlines of 16:06 and 16:09 CDT today are logged.
NLTO, the UMRC and the MN HSEM 06:00 update now give the public the same severity, the same end time and the same customer impact.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. That is the end of play. Put down the phones, close the bridge and step away from the consoles. We'll take ten minutes, then come back together for the hot wash. Bring your logs and the binder tally sheets with you.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline walk-back: go back through the scenario clock from the 22:30 WATA50 watch to the 04:20 termination, stopping at each condition change. At each stop, every role says what they knew, what they did and when. Finish with 3-Up, 3-Down.
hotWashQuestions: Did NLTO apply each condition of the GMD operating procedure before the Kp arrived, or only after it? What made the room act, or wait?

Were all the notification clocks met: the UMRC's 15-minute send, its 30-minute acknowledgment follow-up, and NLTO's 60-minute notice to the 14 entities, both when the procedure started and when it ended? Where did the tally break down, and why?
Was the Iron Range T2 decision made on the record? Can the log show who decided, when, with what data and with which interface schedules?

Did the numbers NLTO gave the public and the media (severity, end time, customers affected) match SWPC, the UMRC and MN HSEM at every point? How did the room handle the G5 rumor, the cyberattack claim and the second-CME rumor?
fields.facilitatorNote: Record these open items for the after-action report: the Iron Range T2 oil result (due 08:00), the review of the Hartley 3H12 trip and the unexplained 3H22 21 Z1 target, the plan for getting Iron Range and Cloquet back on GPS (including the expired ChronoLine Fleet Manager license), and the post-event summary that NGDOP section 8 says must go to the RC within 30 days. Collect evaluator sheets and the players' log and binder pages before the break.
